ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a five-membered ring structure. The ring carbon on the left is connected to two substituents R1 and R2; this ring, starting from the substituted carbon on the left, is connected in sequence to the upper N-H, the right carbonyl carbon C(=O), the ring oxygen O, and then returns to the imine carbon at the bottom. The bottom ring carbon is also connected to an external =N/HN fragment. There are curved arrows in the figure indicating electron transfer, but the problem requires ignoring the arrows. Reasoning: According to the specified method, start encoding from the ring carbon on the left bearing two R groups: one R group is represented by a preceding wildcard, the ring carbon ring-opening number is C1, and the other R group is used as a branch wildcard, so it is *C1(*). Continue along the five-membered ring, passing in sequence through N, the carbonyl carbon C(=O), the ring oxygen O, and then to the ring-closing imine carbon, giving NC(=O)OC1=N. Joining the two parts gives *C1(*)NC(=O)OC1=N.

method.method_draft: Trace the ring from the left substituted carbon. Encode that atom as `*C1(*)` because it has two R-group/wildcard substituents and begins a ring closure. Continue around the ring through N, carbonyl carbon, ring oxygen, and the imine carbon: `NC(=O)OC1=N`. Concatenate these pieces to obtain `*C1(*)NC(=O)OC1=N`.
